ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Why You Buy What You Buy

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
"The truth is that most people are not as (rational / rationally) as they think."

det.ref:
[원문] The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think.
[해석] 사실은 대부분의 사람이 자신들이 생각하는 만큼 합리적이지 않습니다. [문장 04 참고]
det.correct: rational이 정답. as...as 비교 구문에서 be동사(are) 뒤에 보어로 형용사 rational이 와야 합니다. rationally(부사)는 보어로 사용 불가.
wrongs: rationally ❌ — be동사의 보어는 형용사. 부사 rationally는 동사를 수식하므로 부적합.
det.tip:
💡 as + 형용사/부사 + as 비교 구문
• be동사 뒤 → as + 형용사 + as: She is as tall as her mother.
• 일반동사 수식 → as + 부사 + as: He runs as fast as I do.

⚠️ be동사 보어 = 형용사 (부사 불가!)

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
"Human beings are easily (influenced / influencing) by psychological factors."

det.ref:
[원문] Human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors.
[해석] 인간은 심리적인 요인들에 의해 쉽게 영향을 받습니다. [문장 05 참고]
det.correct: influenced가 정답. 주어 Human beings가 영향을 "받는" 대상이므로 수동태(be + p.p.) influenced. by는 수동태의 행위자를 나타냅니다.
wrongs: influencing ❌ — 현재분사는 능동. "인간이 영향을 주는"이 되어 문맥 부적합.
det.tip:
💡 수동태 판별법
• 주어가 동작을 받으면 → be + p.p.
• by + 행위자: influenced by factors

📌 influence 활용
• influence(v./n.): 영향을 주다/영향
• influential(adj.): 영향력 있는
• be influenced by: ~에 의해 영향을 받다

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
"People tend (to rely / relying) on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions."

det.ref:
[원문] people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.
[해석] 사람들은 결정을 내릴 때 처음 접하는 정보에 의존하는 경향이 있습니다. [문장 15 참고]
det.correct: to rely가 정답. tend는 to부정사를 목적어로 취하는 동사입니다. tend to + V: ~하는 경향이 있다.
wrongs: relying ❌ — tend 뒤에 동명사(-ing) 사용 불가. tend to + 동사원형이 고정 표현.
det.tip:
💡 tend to + V (동사원형)
• People tend to forget. (O)
• People tend forgetting. (X)

📌 유사 표현
• be likely to + V: ~할 가능성이 있다
• be inclined to + V: ~하는 성향이 있다
• have a tendency to + V: ~하는 경향이 있다

questions.stem:
(A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
"During the presentation, he said we're going to price it under a thousand dollars, (A)[which / what] most people assumed meant $999. He went on to talk about the features and continued (B)[to justify / justifying] why the tablet was worth (C)[buying / to buy]."

det.ref:
[원문] which most people assumed meant $999. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth buying.
[해석] 대부분의 사람들은 그것이 999달러를 의미한다고 추측했습니다. [문장 08~09 참고]
det.correct:
(A) which — 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사. 콤마+which.
(B) to justify — continue는 to부정사/동명사 둘 다 가능하지만, 여기서는 to justify가 원문.
(C) buying — be worth + V-ing: ~할 가치가 있다. 고정 표현.
wrongs: ② what ❌ — 선행사(앞 절)가 있으므로 what 불가
③ justifying은 가능하나 to buy ❌ — worth + V-ing 고정
④ what+justifying — what 오류
⑤ to buy ❌ — worth buying이 정확
det.tip:
💡 be worth + V-ing (동명사)
• The book is worth reading. (O)
• The book is worth to read. (X)

📌 콤마+which (계속적 용법)
• 앞 문장/절 전체를 선행사로 취함
• He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.

questions.stem:
(A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현은?
"He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning (A)[so that / because] the $499 price would seem a lot (B)[cheaper / more cheaply] in (C)[comparison / comparing]."

det.ref:
[원문] He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in comparison.
[해석] 499달러가 상대적으로 훨씬 저렴해 보이도록 999달러를 초반에 각인시켰습니다. [문장 13 참고]
det.correct:
(A) so that — 목적("~하도록"). 999달러를 심어놓은 목적이 499달러가 저렴해 보이게 하기 위함.
(B) cheaper — seem(2형식 동사) 뒤 보어로 형용사 비교급 cheaper.
(C) comparison — 전치사 in 뒤 명사. in comparison = 비교하여.
wrongs: ② because — 원인이 아닌 목적
③ more cheaply — seem 뒤 형용사, comparing — in 뒤 명사
④ because+cheaply 이중 오류
⑤ comparing — 명사 comparison이 적절
det.tip:
💡 so that + S + would/could/may + V
• 목적: ~하도록, ~하기 위해
• He spoke loudly so that everyone could hear.

📌 seem + 형용사 (보어)
• seem cheap/cheaper (O) — 형용사
• seem cheaply (X) — 부사 불가

questions.stem:
(A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현은?
"The original price serves as an anchor, (A)[making / made] the discounted price appear more reasonable. It is common (B)[for / of] stores (C)[to use / using] this kind of price anchoring."

det.ref:
[원문] making the discounted price appear more reasonable in comparison. It is common for stores to use this kind of price anchoring.
[해석] 할인된 가격을 더 합리적으로 보이게 만듭니다. 상점들이 이런 가격 닻 내림을 사용하는 것은 흔한 일입니다. [문장 25~26 참고]
det.correct:
(A) making — 콤마 뒤 접속사 없이 → 분사구문. 능동이므로 현재분사.
(B) for — 가주어 It...for+의미상주어+to-V 구문. "It is common for stores to use..."
(C) to use — for stores to use: 의미상주어(stores) + to부정사(to use).
wrongs: ② made — 분사구문에서 능동 → making
③ of — It is common for(O), of(X)
④ made+using 이중 오류
⑤ of — for가 적절
det.tip:
💡 가주어 It...for+O+to-V
• It is important for students to study.
• It is common for stores to use...

📌 분사구문 (결과)
• 콤마 뒤 접속사 없이 → V-ing (능동) / V-ed (수동)
• ..., making it appear reasonable (결과)

questions.stem:
밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
In 2010, Steve Jobs ⓐintroduced the tablet computer to the world. He said the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499. The crowd went wild. The tablet suddenly ⓑseemed affordable. He put the price tag in people's minds so that the price ⓒwould seem cheaper. Steve Jobs used something ⓓcalling the anchoring effect. It works because people ⓔtend to rely on the first piece of information.

det.ref:
[원문] Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here.
[해석] 스티브 잡스는 닻 내림 효과라는 것을 유리하게 이용했습니다. [문장 14 참고]
det.correct: ⓓ calling → called. something과 the anchoring effect 사이의 관계가 수동("~라고 불리는")이므로 과거분사 called가 적절. calling은 능동("~라고 부르는").
wrongs: ⓐ introduced ✅ — 과거 시제. 2010년의 사건.
ⓑ seemed ✅ — 과거 시제. 2형식 동사+형용사(affordable).
ⓒ would seem ✅ — so that+would: 목적절의 조동사.
ⓔ tend to rely ✅ — tend to+동사원형. 현재의 일반적 경향.
det.tip:
💡 과거분사 vs 현재분사 (명사 수식)
• called: ~라고 불리는 (수동) → something called X
• calling: ~라고 부르는 (능동) → the person calling you

⚠️ something/anything/nothing + p.p.
• something called, nothing done, anything written

questions.stem:
밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
Only about 10 percent of the students were ⓐwilling to make the exchange. This is because people ⓑvalue something more when they own it. This is the basic idea of the ⓒendowment effect. People are less ⓓlikely to give up ⓔthat they already have.

det.ref:
[원문] People are less likely to give up what they already have or trade it for something else.
[해석] 사람들은 이미 가지고 있는 것을 포기하거나 다른 것으로 교환할 가능성이 낮습니다. [문장 39 참고]
det.correct: ⓔ that → what. give up의 목적어로 "~하는 것"이 필요합니다. 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what(=the thing that)이 적절. that은 선행사가 필요한데 여기에는 없습니다.
wrongs: ⓐ willing ✅ — be willing to: ~할 의향이 있다
ⓑ value ✅ — 동사. 가치 있게 여기다
ⓒ endowment ✅ — 명사. 보유
ⓓ likely ✅ — be likely to: ~할 가능성이 있다
det.tip:
💡 what vs that 핵심 구분
• what = the thing(s) that (선행사 포함)
• that = 선행사가 앞에 필요

📌 give up what S + V
• Give up what you have. (O)
• Give up that you have. (X) — 선행사 없음

⚠️ 빈출 함정: what/that/which 혼동

questions.stem:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
The crowd went wild. The tablet suddenly seemed ①affordable to everyone. He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in ②comparison. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his ③disadvantage here. It works because people tend to ④rely on the first piece of ⑤information they receive.

det.ref:
[원문] Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here.
[해석] 스티브 잡스는 닻 내림 효과를 유리하게 이용했습니다. [문장 14 참고]
det.correct: ③ disadvantage(불리함)가 부적절. 원문은 advantage(유리함). 잡스가 닻 내림 효과를 "유리하게" 활용했으므로 disadvantage는 정반대.
wrongs: ① affordable ✅ — 구매할 만한 가격의. 적절.
② comparison ✅ — in comparison: 비교하여. 적절.
④ rely ✅ — rely on: ~에 의존하다. 적절.
⑤ information ✅ — 정보. 적절.
det.tip:
💡 반의어 함정
• advantage(유리함) ↔ disadvantage(불리함)
• to one's advantage: ~에게 유리하게
• to one's disadvantage: ~에게 불리하게

📌 문맥 판단: 잡스는 효과를 성공적으로 활용 → advantage

questions.stem:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
Companies often use the endowment effect as a ①marketing strategy. Many media streaming companies ②offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ③ownership of that service. ④Consequently, they are likely to value it more and are ⑤reluctant to pay to continue to own it.

det.ref:
[원문] Consequently, they are likely to value it more and are willing to pay to continue to own it.
[해석] 결과적으로 그것을 좀 더 가치 있게 여기게 되고 기꺼이 돈을 지불합니다. [문장 43 참고]
det.correct: ⑤ reluctant(꺼리는)이 부적절. 원문은 willing(기꺼이 하는). 보유 효과로 고객이 "기꺼이" 돈을 내므로 reluctant은 정반대.
wrongs: ① marketing ✅ — 마케팅 전략. 적절.
② offer ✅ — 제공하다. 적절.
③ ownership ✅ — 소유권. 적절.
④ Consequently ✅ — 결과적으로. 적절.
det.tip:
💡 반의어 함정
• willing(기꺼이 하는) ↔ reluctant(꺼리는)
• be willing to: ~할 의향이 있다
• be reluctant to: ~하기를 꺼리다

📌 보유 효과 핵심: 소유→가치 상승→돈 지불 의향↑

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 모두 찾아 바르게 고친 것은?
"Let's say you are shopping for a new jacket and the first one you see are priced at $100. That's too expensive, as you don't want to spending more than $50. You see a similar jacket with a $70 price tag. You think it's affordable, even though the price is still beyond your budget."

det.ref:
[원문] the first one you see is priced at $100. you don't want to spend more than $50. even though the price is still beyond your budget.
[해석] 처음에 본 것이 100달러. 50달러 이상 쓰고 싶지 않다. 가격이 여전히 예산을 초과한다. [문장 16~19 참고]
det.correct:
2가지 오류:
① are → is: the first one(단수)이 주어이므로 단수동사 is.
② spending → spend: want to + 동사원형. to 뒤에 -ing 불가.
wrongs: ② beyond→within은 원문 그대로(예산을 초과)이므로 오류 아님
③ beyond은 정상
④ 3개는 과다 수정
⑤ 1개만으로 불완전
det.tip:
💡 want to + 동사원형
• want to spend (O) / want to spending (X)

📌 수일치: the first one = 단수
• one이 주어 → is

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 모두 찾아 바르게 고친 것은?
"In an experiment, one group of students were given a coffee mug. Both groups were told they could exchange their items. A third group wasn't given something and was told to choose both a chocolate bar or a coffee mug."

det.ref:
[원문] one group of students was given a coffee mug. A third group wasn't given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug.
[해석] 첫 번째 그룹에게는 커피잔을, 세 번째 그룹에게는 아무것도 주지 않고 선택하게 했습니다. [문장 28~30 참고]
det.correct:
3가지 오류:
① were → was: one group(단수)이 주어. of students는 전치사구.
② something → anything: 부정문(wasn't given)에서는 anything.
③ both → either: either A or B 구문. both A and B와 혼동 주의.
wrongs: ② 2개만 — both→either 누락
③ 2개만 — were→was 누락
④ 2개만 — something→anything 누락
det.tip:
💡 수일치: one group of students → 단수(was)

📌 부정문에서 some → any
• not...anything (O) / not...something (X)

📌 either A or B vs both A and B
• choose either A or B: A 또는 B 중 선택
• choose both A and B: A와 B 둘 다 선택

questions.passage: Most people are not as rational as they think. ( ___ ) human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 표현을 쓰시오. (4단어, T로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] This is because human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors.
[해석] 인간은 심리적인 요인들에 의해 쉽게 영향을 받기 때문이죠. [문장 04~05 참고]
det.correct: This is because가 정답. 앞 문장의 현상(비합리적)에 대한 이유(심리적 요인)를 설명하는 인과 표현.
det.tip:
💡 This is because + 이유(원인)
• 앞: 결과/현상 → 뒤: 원인/이유
• This is because people tend to...

📌 cf. This is why + 결과
• 앞: 원인 → 뒤: 결과

questions.passage: Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership. ( ___ ), they are likely to value it more.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 13자, C로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] Consequently, they are likely to value it more and are willing to pay to continue to own it.
[해석] 결과적으로 그것을 좀 더 가치 있게 여기게 됩니다. [문장 42~43 참고]
det.correct: Consequently가 정답. 원인(소유감) → 결과(가치 상승). 인과/결과 관계.
det.tip:
💡 결과 연결사
• Consequently: 결과적으로 (격식)
• As a result: 그 결과
• Therefore: 따라서
• Thus: 그러므로

questions.passage: You think it is affordable, ( ___ ) the price is still beyond your budget.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 표현을 쓰시오. (2단어, e로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] You think it's affordable, even though the price is still beyond your budget.
[해석] 가격이 여전히 예산을 초과하지만, 적당한 가격이라고 생각합니다. [문장 19 참고]
det.correct: even though가 정답. "적당하다고 생각" vs "예산 초과" — 양보(역접) 관계.
det.tip:
💡 양보 접속사
• even though + S + V: ~임에도 불구하고 (사실)
• although/though: ~이지만
• cf. even if: ~일지라도 (가정)

📌 even though vs even if
• even though: 확실한 사실
• even if: 불확실한 가정

questions.passage: The truth is that most people are not as ( ___ ) as they think.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 8자, r로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think.
[해석] 사실 대부분의 사람이 자신들이 생각하는 만큼 합리적이지 않습니다. [문장 04 참고]
det.correct: rational이 정답. 합리적인. as...as 비교 구문에서 be동사 보어로 형용사.
det.tip:
💡 rational 파생어
• rational(adj.): 합리적인
• rationally(adv.): 합리적으로
• irrational(adj.): 비합리적인
• rationalize(v.): 합리화하다

questions.passage: The first piece of information acts as an ( ___ ) that influences your decisions later.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 6자, a로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] the first piece of information acts as an anchor that influences your decisions later.

questions.passage:
Good afternoon, students. Today, I'd like to talk about a topic that concerns us all: Money! Do you think that you spend money wisely? The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think. This is because human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors. Let me illustrate my point through the following examples.

The Anchoring Effect
In 2010, Steve Jobs introduced the tablet computer to the world. During the presentation, he said, "We're going to price it under a thousand dollars," which most people assumed meant $999. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth buying. At the end, he said, "I am thrilled to announce to you that the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499." The crowd went wild. The tablet suddenly seemed affordable to everyone. He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in comparison. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here. It works because people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.

Let's say you are shopping for a new jacket and the first one you see is priced at $100. That's too expensive, as you don't want to spend more than $50. Soon after, you see a similar jacket from a different brand with a $70 price tag. You think it's affordable, even though the price is still beyond your budget. This is because the first piece of information acts as an anchor that influences your decisions later.

Here's another common example. Look at the two pairs of sneakers. They both are $50, but the way their price is presented is different. Naturally, people are more drawn to the second pair. This is because the original price serves as an anchor, making the discounted price appear more reasonable in comparison. It is common for stores to use this kind of price anchoring as a way to encourage purchases.

The Endowment Effect
Now let's move on to another interesting effect. In an experiment, one group of students was given a coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could exchange their items. A third group wasn't given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an equal preference for the two items. About half of the group chose the chocolate bar, and the other half chose the coffee mug. This suggested that roughly half of the first and second groups would trade their items. But that's not what happened. Only about 10 percent of the students in the first and second groups were willing to make the exchange. Why is this? This is because people value something more when they own it. This is the basic idea of the endowment effect. People are less likely to give up what they already have or trade it for something else.

Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy. For example, many media streaming companies offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership of that service, even if it's temporary. Consequently, they are likely to value it more and are willing to pay to continue to own it. A free-return policy is another example. Say that a company is offering free returns on a smartwatch within 30 days of purchase. It seems like a good deal, since you can get a refund even after using the item. But once you take this deal and establish ownership of the watch, it is unlikely that you will return it.

As we've seen, our spending can be influenced by factors that appeal to our emotions and mind. I hope this short lecture gave you a chance to reflect on your own spending and helped you understand the reasons behind irrational purchasing decisions.
questions.stem:
본문의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고른 것으로 옳은 것은?
(가) 스티브 잡스는 태블릿 가격을 처음에 $499로 공개했다.
(나) 닻 내림 효과는 사람들이 처음 접한 정보에 의존하는 경향을 이용한다.
(다) 보유 효과 실험에서 세 번째 그룹은 두 물건에 균등한 선호를 보였다.
(라) 첫 번째와 두 번째 그룹의 약 50%가 물건을 교환했다.
(마) 무료 반품 정책은 보유 효과를 이용한 마케팅 전략이다.

det.ref: 본문 전체 참고
det.correct:
(가)F — 처음 $999를 먼저 언급 후 $499 공개 [문장 08,10]
(나)T — "people tend to rely on the first piece of information" [문장 15]
(다)T — "equal preference for the two items" [문장 31]
(라)F — 약 10%만 교환 의향, 50% 아님 [문장 35]
(마)T — "A free-return policy is another example" [문장 44]
wrongs: ② (가)T ❌ — $999 먼저 언급
③ (나)F ❌ — 본문에 명시
④ (다)F+(라)T ❌ — 본문과 반대
⑤ (마)F ❌ — 본문에 명시
det.tip:
💡 T/F 풀이: 숫자/비율 함정 주의
• $999 먼저 → $499 나중 (순서 함정)
• 10% vs 50% (비율 함정)

questions.passage:
Good afternoon, students. Today, I'd like to talk about a topic that concerns us all: Money! Do you think that you spend money wisely? The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think. This is because human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors. Let me illustrate my point through the following examples.

The Anchoring Effect
In 2010, Steve Jobs introduced the tablet computer to the world. During the presentation, he said, "We're going to price it under a thousand dollars," which most people assumed meant $999. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth buying. At the end, he said, "I am thrilled to announce to you that the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499." The crowd went wild. The tablet suddenly seemed affordable to everyone. He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in comparison. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here. It works because people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.

Let's say you are shopping for a new jacket and the first one you see is priced at $100. That's too expensive, as you don't want to spend more than $50. Soon after, you see a similar jacket from a different brand with a $70 price tag. You think it's affordable, even though the price is still beyond your budget. This is because the first piece of information acts as an anchor that influences your decisions later.

Here's another common example. Look at the two pairs of sneakers. They both are $50, but the way their price is presented is different. Naturally, people are more drawn to the second pair. This is because the original price serves as an anchor, making the discounted price appear more reasonable in comparison. It is common for stores to use this kind of price anchoring as a way to encourage purchases.

The Endowment Effect
Now let's move on to another interesting effect. In an experiment, one group of students was given a coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could exchange their items. A third group wasn't given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an equal preference for the two items. About half of the group chose the chocolate bar, and the other half chose the coffee mug. This suggested that roughly half of the first and second groups would trade their items. But that's not what happened. Only about 10 percent of the students in the first and second groups were willing to make the exchange. Why is this? This is because people value something more when they own it. This is the basic idea of the endowment effect. People are less likely to give up what they already have or trade it for something else.

Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy. For example, many media streaming companies offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership of that service, even if it's temporary. Consequently, they are likely to value it more and are willing to pay to continue to own it. A free-return policy is another example. Say that a company is offering free returns on a smartwatch within 30 days of purchase. It seems like a good deal, since you can get a refund even after using the item. But once you take this deal and establish ownership of the watch, it is unlikely that you will return it.

As we've seen, our spending can be influenced by factors that appeal to our emotions and mind. I hope this short lecture gave you a chance to reflect on your own spending and helped you understand the reasons behind irrational purchasing decisions.

③ financial ❌ — 재정적. 결과이지 원인 아님.
